title: From proposal to contract — the ladder of section 2

steps.title: Proposal (offer)
steps.text: Willingness to do or abstain, made to obtain the other's assent — specific or general

steps.title: Acceptance
steps.text: Absolute, unqualified, communicated, in the prescribed or a reasonable manner

steps.title: Promise
steps.text: A proposal, when accepted, becomes a promise; promisor and promisee

steps.title: Consideration
steps.text: At the desire of the promisor, by the promisee or any other person — past, present or future

steps.title: Agreement
steps.text: Every promise and every set of promises forming consideration for each other

steps.title: Enforceable by law = CONTRACT
steps.text: Free consent · competent parties · lawful consideration and object · not expressly void · any required form

root: Section 25 — an agreement without consideration is VOID, unless…
rootSub: In any of these cases the agreement is a contract

children.title: (1) Natural love and affection
bullets: Made on account of natural love and affection

children.title: (2) Past voluntary service
bullets: For the promisor, or what he was legally compellable to do
Promise to compensate wholly or in part

children.title: (3) Time-barred debt
bullets: Promise to pay wholly or in part
In writing, signed by debtor or agent
Illus. (e): Rs. 500 of a barred Rs. 1,000

children.title: Explanation 1 — completed gift
children.text: A gift actually made is valid between donor and donee without consideration

children.title: Explanation 2 — inadequacy
children.text: Inadequate consideration does not void the agreement; it is evidence on whether consent was free (illus. (f), (g))

children.title: Elsewhere in the Act
children.text: Agency needs no consideration (s. 185); gratuitous bailment; surety (s. 127); remission (s. 63)

title: The minor's position under the Contract Act — at a glance

cards.title: Void ab initio
cards.text: No contract at all; cannot be enforced against the minor (Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose)

cards.title: No refund under ss. 64–65
cards.text: Those sections assume competent parties; s. 41 SRA relief is discretionary

cards.title: No ratification
cards.text: Nothing to ratify on majority; a fresh promise needs fresh consideration

cards.title: No estoppel
cards.text: A lie about age does not bind him (Sadiq Ali Khan v. Jai Kishori; Art. 114 QSO)

cards.title: Restitution in equity
cards.text: Benefits obtained by fraud may be ordered restored (Khan Gul v. Lakha Singh, Lahore FB)

cards.title: No specific performance
cards.text: Not against him, nor by him — no mutuality (Mir Sarwarjan)

cards.title: Can be a beneficiary
cards.text: Promisee, payee, mortgagee; can enforce where he has performed

cards.title: Agent / partner
cards.text: May be an agent (s. 184); admitted to benefits of partnership (s. 30 PA)

cards.title: Necessaries (s. 68)
cards.text: Supplier reimbursed from the minor's property — no personal liability

root: Consent is FREE when not caused by…
rootSub: s. 14 — 'caused' means the consent would not have been given but for the defect

children.title: Coercion — s. 15
bullets: PPC act, or unlawful detention of property

children.title: Fraud — s. 17
bullets: Knowingly false; active concealment; promise without intent
Silence only if duty to speak
Voidable or affirm; damages in deceit

children.title: Misrepresentation — s. 18
bullets: Breach of duty; causing mistake of substance

children.title: No consent at all — s. 13
bullets: Not the same thing in the same sense

title: Section 23 — consideration or object is unlawful if it…

cards.title: 1. Is forbidden by law
cards.text: Statute prohibits it expressly or by implication — illus. (f): buying a public-service job

cards.title: 2. Would defeat any law
cards.text: Lawful on its face but evades a statute — illus. (i): defaulter buying back through B

cards.title: 3. Is fraudulent
cards.text: Illus. (e): dividing gains of fraud; (g): agent's secret lease deal

cards.title: 4. Injures person or property
cards.text: Wrongful act — defamation, trespass, bonded labour

cards.title: 5. Is immoral
cards.text: Illus. (j): mukhtar selling influence; (k): concubinage

cards.title: 6. Opposes public policy
cards.text: Stifling prosecution (illus. (h)), trading with the enemy, interfering with justice — 'an unruly horse'

title: Agreements the Act expressly declares void

cards.title: s. 26 — Restraint of marriage
cards.text: Of any person other than a minor

cards.title: s. 27 — Restraint of trade
cards.text: Any restraint, total or partial; only the goodwill-sale exception within reasonable local limits

cards.title: s. 28 — Restraint of legal proceedings
cards.text: Absolute bar or shortened limitation; arbitration agreements saved

cards.title: s. 29 — Uncertainty
cards.text: Meaning not certain or capable of being made certain

cards.title: s. 30 — Wagers
cards.text: No suit for winnings or stakes; horse-race prize of Rs. 500+ saved; s. 294A PPC preserved

cards.title: ss. 30A–30C — Collateral to wagers (Pakistan, 1960)
cards.text: Collateral agreements void; no suit for commission; no credit to guardians / executors

cards.title: Also void
cards.text: No consideration (s. 25); partly unlawful (s. 24); bilateral mistake (s. 20); impossible act (s. 56); impossible event (s. 36)

cards.title: Incapacity
cards.text: Minors and persons of unsound mind (ss. 11–12; Mohori Bibee)

title: Modes of discharge of a contract

root.title: Discharge of contract
root.sub: how the obligations come to an end

children.title: Agreement
children.sub: s. 62 novation, rescission, alteration · s. 63 remission

cards.title: s. 68 — Necessaries
cards.text: Supplied to an incapable person or his dependants — reimbursed from his property

cards.title: s. 69 — Interested payer
cards.text: Pays money another is bound by law to pay, to protect his own interest — reimbursed

cards.title: s. 70 — Non-gratuitous act
cards.text: Lawful act, not intended as gratuitous, benefit enjoyed — compensate (B.K. Mondal)

cards.title: s. 71 — Finder of goods
cards.text: Same responsibility as a bailee; rights under ss. 168–169

cards.title: s. 72 — Mistake or coercion
cards.text: Money paid or thing delivered must be returned; mistake includes law (Kanhaiya Lal Saraf)

cards.title: s. 73, para 3 — Compensation
cards.text: Failure to discharge such an obligation is compensated as if a contract had been broken

root: How important is the term that was broken?
rootSub: the class of term decides the remedy

children.title: Innominate term
bullets: Terminate only if deprived of substantially the whole benefit

title: The five-step method for a contract problem

steps.title: Formation
steps.text: Offer, acceptance, communication, revocation, consideration, intention

steps.title: Validity
steps.text: Capacity, free consent, lawful object, expressly void, form

steps.title: Performance and discharge
steps.text: Performed or tendered? Excused? Time of the essence?

steps.title: Breach
steps.text: Actual or anticipatory; repudiation accepted or not

steps.title: Remedy
steps.text: Damages, penalty, rescission, restitution, specific performance, injunction
